newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends firmer in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends firmer in quiet market.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against the U.S. unit on Monday in featureless trade.
The Taiwan dollar ended at T$27.491 versus T$27.495 at the Staturday's close. Turnover was a moderate US$192.5 million.

After a soft opening, the Taiwan dollar edged up in fairly routine trade. Selling of U.S. dollars by exporters was offset by importers' buying. Purchase of the Taiwan dollar by foreign funds was negligible, dealers said. "It's Monday and we usually get some importers business, but the business was slow today," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "We seldom have days of over $200 million (of turnover) in recent months," she added.
What held back today's activity was also attributed to the nervousness ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday, said another dealer.

If the Fed leaves the monetary policy unchanged, instead of hiking the Fed funds rate by 25 basis points as expected by a slim majority of U.S. economists, the U.S. dollar could ease a notch, nudging the Taiwan dollar higher, he said.
Any U.S. dollar movement, however, is unlikely to jolt the Taiwan dollar out of its recent narrow range, the first dealer said. -- Nailene Chou Wiest (2-5080815)
